chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Sallam, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdurrahman, from al-Khashshab, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) from his fathers (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The example of my family is like the stars of the sky; whenever a star sets, another rises. Until when a star from them sets and rises, you glance at it with your eyes and point to it with your fingers, the Angel of Death comes to it and takes it away. Then you remain in that state for a period of time from your lifespan, and the children of Abdul Muttalib become equal and it is not known which is which. At that time, your star will appear, so praise Allah and accept it."

key_terms.نَجْمُكُمْ: Your star (referring to the specific Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of the stars used to describe the succession of the Imams in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawatur* (continuous succession) among the Twelve Imams, using the celestial metaphor of stars to signify their infallible guidance and enduring presence. The 'period of indistinguishability' refers to the *Ghaybat al-Kubra* (Major Occultation), where the lineage of Banu Hashim remains obscured until the Mahdi emerges, a transition marked by the shift from visible recognition to faithful acceptance. This narrative underscores the theological certainty of the Imamate's continuity despite political obscurity, a key theme in Usuli scholarship.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Ali bin Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi from Musa bin Sallam from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr from Abdurrahman from al-Khashshab from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) from his fathers (as) that the Prophet (S) had said:

“The example of my family is like the stars of the sky. Whenever a star sets another shines until a certain star shines and you glance at it and point at it with your fingers then the Angel of Death comes to take it (him) with him. After that you remain a period of time. The progeny of Abdul Muttalib become the same in this regard and none will be distinguished from the other then your star will reappear. Praise Allah and accept it!”
